$comment: PER-RUNG FIELD OVERRIDES. The second override point between the committed
`metal` tree and what CI actually syncs; the first is the resource rung,
Aaron 2026-09-04: 'metal is just for hardware and hopeuflly they just
diverge between dev and metal is disk, cpu, memory, etc... request maybe
replica counts but i'd love to try to test everyting in CI', and on the GPU
specifically 'yes on real metal we can add any gpu selectors'.
So an entry here must encode a SUBSTRATE FACT -- something the CI runner
physically does not have and the hardware does -- never a preference and
never a convenience. A GitHub runner has no GPU; the 16-core box does.
These are applied to a STAGED COPY by lane-tree-source and never to the
committed tree, so the hardware box keeps `metal` byte-for-byte.
EVERY ENTRY MUST DO SOMETHING: `applyRungOverrides` THROWS when an override
produces zero edits, because a no-op override reads as coverage and buys
none. Every entry also carries a `reason` and a `liftsWhen`, and the loader
refuses an entry missing either, or naming a rung the catalogue lacks.

overrides.reason: OLLAMA IS CPU-CAPABLE WITH THE SAME IMAGE; the GPU is opt-in. The committed tree is `metal`, where `ollama.gpu.enabled: true`, `nodeSelector: {zeta.io/gpu: nvidia}` and an `nvidia.com/gpu: 1` request are all correct -- that box has the card. A GitHub-hosted runner does not, which is a substrate fact rather than a preference, and it is the whole of why this Application had no expressible dev form before this file existed. Turning the GPU off, dropping the selector and replacing the requests map (which is how the `nvidia.com/gpu` key is removed at all -- its name contains dots, so no dotted path can address it) leaves an ordinary CPU server. `replicaCount` goes 0 -> 1 because a zero-replica Application reaches Healthy while scheduling nothing, which Aaron named exactly: 'it's half a test of the chart but not the pod/continer'. The dev sizing is 250m/512Mi, not the metal 2/8Gi: the model pull and run lists are EMPTY, so what starts is an idle server process, and 2000m would take a third of the lane's whole CPU budget for a process doing nothing.
overrides.liftsWhen: a GPU-bearing self-hosted runner serves this lane, at which point dev and metal want the same values and this entry is deleted rather than edited.

overrides.reason: OPENSEARCH REFUSES TO BOOT WITH THE SECURITY PLUGIN ON AND NO ADMIN PASSWORD, and that is why the live lane reported OutOfSync/Progressing on run 33936923932. FOUND BY READING UPSTREAM'S OWN CI, which is the cheapest possible source of truth: opensearch-project/helm-charts runs `helm/kind-action` + `ct install` on ubuntu-latest, so this chart IS expected to install on a GitHub runner -- and ALL THREE of its `charts/opensearch/ci/*-values.yaml` files set `OPENSEARCH_INITIAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD`. The stock `values.yaml` has that line COMMENTED OUT (line 110) while shipping `securityConfig.enabled: true` and `protocol: https`, so a chart taken at its defaults cannot start. THE DEV FIX IS TO TURN SECURITY OFF, NOT TO COMMIT A PASSWORD: this repository is PUBLIC, and a literal admin credential in a values file is a credential in git forever. A smoke-test index needs no TLS and no user database. `metal` keeps `securityConfig.enabled: true` and https untouched, where the password belongs in a minted Secret beside the Grafana admin one.
overrides.liftsWhen: the dev lane mints an OpenSearch admin Secret the way `applyDevBootstrapSecrets` already mints Grafana's, at which point dev can run the same security posture as metal and this entry is deleted.
